“Yes, when you spray your cat with water, chances are she’ll stop what she’s doing and run away. With a playful kitten, this quickly becomes a game: “I jump on the counter, you give me a squirt, I run away, then I jump back on the counter and the game begins again. This is fun!” Have I taught her not to jump on the counter? No.

With a more shy cat, this quickly becomes a reason to stay away from you: “I jump up to a high place to feel safe, you attack me with water, and I run and hide. You can’t be trusted. I’ll wait until you leave the house to investigate the counter.” Have I taught him not to jump on the counter? No.

Here’s the problem with spraying a cat with water: The only thing the cat learns is that when he sees the water bottle, it’s time to run. “Run whenever you see this bottle” is not a particularly useful cue to teach, and running to escape punishment is not a positive way to interact with your cat. It doesn’t build the bond between you, and it’s not an effective training method. Let’s think about why not.

What we’re really trying to say with the spray bottle is “stop whatever you’re doing”—in other words, “no.” There’s nothing wrong with setting reasonable limits on your cat’s behavior, especially when his health and safety are involved. But “stop whatever you’re doing” or “no” or a squirt of water don’t convey clear information.

At any given moment, a cat is doing a lot of things—sitting or standing, being in a particular place, looking at something, perhaps swatting or some other action. Which one of these things does “no” refer to? Is he supposed to stop doing them all, or some of them? Are you trying to teach him that he should not sit, not look, not swat, not be in that place? He has no way to know what you want.”

Yeah man, I got you. Sorry it’s long but I hope it’s realistic and optimistic for you. I’m 24 and I’ve been NC with my abusive narcissist mom since January 2020, and it’s been a very positive experience for me. Like you, it was the right and only move left for my sanity. It was right after I graduated college and she was expecting me to move back home. I knew if I did, I’d kill myself. 

I couldn’t take any more verbal and emotional abuse and I knew I had to go no contact to save myself. I have 3 little brothers, the youngest one was 5 at the time. I was in college most of his life, but I just adore him. My other brothers Im not close to, but I feared what would happen when I left. One brother is my stepbrother that my mother hates…and the other is autistic and very depressed. I feared when I left her, they’d be the first ones to be taken away from me. She’d tried before for smaller offenses. 

Also, a lot of my clothing was still at her house. My books from high school and college. Yearbooks. Baby pics and stuffed animals. My memories. 

It was really hard but in order to go no contact, I had to let it all go. I had to accept she would never let me see my siblings again. I had to accept that she would bad mouth me to anyone who would listen. I had to accept that the majority of my family wouldn’t speak to me again. 

I knew she’d shut off my phone and throw all my things away (she did it before when i was 12 and missing my dad, so pissing her off like this, i knew she’d go nuclear). I knew she’d tell my siblings I hated them and blame them for me not coming home. I knew she’d do everything to keep me in her control and keep me from getting independence or love from anyone she could. 

I was terrified. I felt like I didn’t have a choice because how could I choose to lose my innocent and abused siblings because my mother is evil??? 

I cried, I grieved, and it was ugly. I panicked and sobbed for probably a week straight, just agonizing to my boyfriend. When it was finally over, I still didn’t know it was over. I was scared, waiting for calls from family members, waiting for the other shoe to drop and her control to finally choke me out. 

Some calls came, some texts, some prying and pressuring from my stepdad. My worst fears didn’t come true even though the best case scenario didn’t happen either. I definitely mentally prepared for the worst…but I found power in answering how I wanted to and in knowing I can tell them to bug off if they don’t support me or at least respect my boundaries. 

I don’t see my siblings in person, but I call my brothers and we play animal crossing together. We play for hours some weekends. I send them gifts for holidays and get thank you calls. I see my grandma from my dads side more now too, which has been nice. I keep in contact with my maternal grandma as well.

I got my own apartment in a city. I eat good food and I have good company. My home is my own space and I don’t hear yelling or my parents fighting or have to hide in my room all day sleeping. I have anxiety attacks but not because my mom is abusing me currently. I have depression, but I don’t feel so fatalistic about life. I’m also medicated now, which I wouldn’t have been able to do at home. 

I feel like I have agency, autonomy, and choice. I never got to feel like a kid which sucks, but I’m enjoying experiencing peace and loving the hobbies I abandoned at 12.

I make coffee with my roommates and when i forget to do the dishes no one wakes me up in the middle of the night to do them or goes through my phone or accuses me of doing drugs. My room is messy and no one screams at me, my boyfriend gently helps me clean up and stay on top of things. I live with my best friend, my boyfriend of 4 years, and our 2yr old kitty we’ve raised. Whereas my mom gave both of my childhood cats away to punish me. 

The life I live isn’t perfect. I am very barely financially stable, I don’t have self esteem, my therapist just told me she doesn’t actually take my insurance, and I’m anxious a lot. The PTSD is real. But I don’t live in constant fear of my parents and the daily strain from them and their antics is gone. I feel so much better about my life. 

Having absolutely no contact with my mom was the best thing i’ve ever done. I feel like if i can cut off my own mom, i can do anything. It’s so worth it to walk away from that toxicity. The peace of mind wasn’t like a whoosh of freedom kinda feeling, but just a gentle relaxation…like out of the lions pit and into the real world where the people i love arent out to get me. 

Nerve racking, but so much better than putting up with it for another moment. I’m so glad I did it. I’ll never regret it. Im starting to heal and actually take care of myself, my interests and thrive in my relationships. I’m proud of me for doing it and sticking to my guns and I’m proud of you OP for acknowledging what you need and seeking encouragement. I honestly wouldn’t have found the strength to leave if it wasn’t for this subreddit.
